court: In the High Court of Madras
judges_raw: (Before Anita Sumanth and Sunder Mohan, JJ.)
respondents: Government of Tamilnadu, Rep. By its, Addl. Chief Secretary to Govt. and Others … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Petitioner(s): Mr. Vinoth Kumar for Mr. A. Vijayasankar
For Respondent(s): Mr. R. Muniyapparaj Additional Public Prosecutor Assisted By Mr. M. Sylvester John
prayer: PRAYER: Petition filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India for issuance of writ of Habeas Corpus to call for the entire records culminating in the Passing of the order of detention the petitioner's Husband of the detenue under Act 1982 as Drug Offender vide detention order in BBCDEFGISSSV No. 99/2025 dated 14-8-2025 on the file of the 2nd respondent herein and quash the same as direct and person of the detenue by name Arun, male, Age 34, Son of Soundarpandian, before this Court and set him at liberty. The detention now contained at Central Prison, Puzhal.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Anita Sumanth, J.:— Challenging the order of detention dated 14-8-2025, this HCP has been filed by the wife of the detenu, who was branded as Drug Offender under Section 2(e) of the Tamil Nadu Preventive Detention Act, 1982 (in short “Act”).

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner points out to various infirmities in the impugned order of detention emphasising on the fact that the Special Report of the Inspector of Police is undated.

3. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondents.

4. The detenu was arrested on 17-7-2025 and the order of detention has been passed on 14-8-2025. Upon perusal of the booklet, we find that the Special Report is not even dated. The Special Report is an important document on the basis of which the detaining authority proceeds to pass the order of detention.

5. The order of detention must be based on cogent and authenticated material to enable the authority to form subjective satisfaction that the order of detention is necessitated.

6. Hence, we are of the considered view that an undated Special Report would not serve as cogent material, sufficient to sustain an order of preventive detention.

7. Since the Special Report in this case is, admittedly, undated, and has been relied upon by the detaining authority, as a sequitur, the impugned order of detention is liable to be quashed.

8. Accordingly, this Habeas Corpus Petition is allowed and the Detention Order passed by the second respondent in BBCDEFGISSSV No. 99/2025, dated 14-8-2025 is set aside.

9. The detenu viz. S. Arun, S/o. Soundara Pandian, aged 34 years, who is now confined in Central Prison, Puzhal, Chennai, is directed to be set at liberty forthwith unless his presence is required in connection with any other case.
